title: Trying choices and backtracking: saving paths to 7
summary: Append each node to path on entry and pop it on exit; copy and save path on each of the two matches with 7, leaving path empty when the search ends.
context: The parent-child relationships of the fixed tree are shown in the table below. The left 7 is the left child of root 1, and the right 7 is the right child of node 3.
Traverse the entire tree in "root → left → right" preorder to find the paths from root node 1 to every node with value 7.

The state list path maintains the active path from the root to the current node in real time, and the result list res stores a copy of path each time a 7 is matched. The figure abbreviates path and res using node values, whereas the accompanying code stores node objects and list copies list(path); the left and right nodes with value 7 are distinct objects.
description: Each forward "trial" entering a node appends it to the end of path; if the current node has value 7, a copy of path is appended to res; before "backtracking" out of a node, it is popped from the end of path to restore the path from before entering that node.
result: Because res stores independent list copies of path taken at each match, popping during backtracking modifies only the active path without altering previously saved solutions.

frames.title: Enter root 1
frames.explanation: Start at root node 1 and append 1 to path. Node value 1 is not the target 7, so path = [1] and res = []; both subtrees remain to be explored, and the search next enters the left 7.
frames.announcement: Enter root node 1 and append 1 to path.

frames.title: Match left 7 and save path
frames.explanation: Enter the left 7 from root 1, append 7, and match the target, saving a copy of the current path to res. Now path = [1, 7] and res = [[1, 7]]; continue exploring the left 7's children 4 and 5.
frames.key_state: Matched left 7; path = [1, 7], and after copying and saving, res = [[1, 7]].
frames.announcement: Visit the left node 7 and save path copy [1, 7] to res.

frames.title: Enter node 4
frames.explanation: Enter the left leaf node 4 of the left 7 and append 4 to path; it is not the target 7. Now path = [1, 7, 4] and res = [[1, 7]]; node 5 and the root's right subtree remain to be explored.
frames.announcement: Enter left leaf node 4, updating path to [1, 7, 4].

frames.title: Exit 4 and return to left 7
frames.explanation: Both empty subtrees of leaf node 4 have returned, so pop 4 from path and return to its parent, the left 7. Now path = [1, 7] and res = [[1, 7]]; node 4 is finished, and the right child 5 is explored next.
frames.key_state: Popped 4 and backtracked to left 7; path is restored to [1, 7], res = [[1, 7]].
frames.announcement: Backtrack from leaf node 4 and pop 4, restoring path to [1, 7].

frames.title: Enter node 5
frames.explanation: Enter the right leaf node 5 of the left 7 and append 5 to path; the previously popped sibling node 4 does not linger. Now path = [1, 7, 5] and res = [[1, 7]]; all nodes in the left subtree have been visited, and the root's right subtree remains to be explored.
frames.announcement: Enter right leaf node 5, updating path to [1, 7, 5].

frames.title: Exit 5 and left 7
frames.explanation: After finishing node 5, first pop 5 to return to the left 7; since both of its subtrees are now complete, pop the left 7 as well to return to root 1. This frame combines those two backtracking steps. Now path = [1] and res = [[1, 7]]; next explore the root's right child 3.
frames.key_state: Popped 5 and left 7 in succession to return to root 1; path is restored to [1], while res remains [[1, 7]].
frames.announcement: Exit node 5 and left 7 in succession, restoring path to [1].

frames.title: Enter node 3
frames.explanation: Enter the right child 3 of root 1 and append 3 to path; it is not the target 7. Now path = [1, 3] and res = [[1, 7]]; continue exploring node 3's left leaf 6 and right leaf 7.
frames.announcement: Enter the root's right child 3, updating path to [1, 3].

frames.title: Enter node 6
frames.explanation: Enter the left leaf node 6 of node 3 and append 6 to path; it is not the target 7. Now path = [1, 3, 6] and res = [[1, 7]]; across the whole tree, only node 3's right child 7 remains unvisited.
frames.announcement: Enter left leaf node 6, updating path to [1, 3, 6].

frames.title: Exit 6 and return to 3
frames.explanation: Leaf node 6 is finished, so pop 6 from path and return to parent node 3. Now path = [1, 3] and res = [[1, 7]]; node 6 is complete, and the right 7 is explored next.
frames.key_state: Popped 6 and backtracked to node 3; path is restored to [1, 3], res = [[1, 7]].
frames.announcement: Backtrack from leaf node 6 and pop 6, restoring path to [1, 3].

frames.title: Match right 7 and save path
frames.explanation: Enter the right leaf node 7 of node 3, append 7 to match the second target node, and save a copy of path to res. Now path = [1, 3, 7] and res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]]; all nodes have been visited, leaving only the final cleanup backtracking.
frames.key_state: Matched right 7; path = [1, 3, 7], and after copying and saving, res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]].
frames.announcement: Visit the right node 7 and save the second path copy [1, 3, 7] to res.

frames.title: Exit right 7, 3, and root 1
frames.explanation: After finishing the right 7, pop the right 7, parent node 3, and root 1 from path in order. This frame combines the three final backtracking steps, ending the search with path = [] and res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]]; the saved copies remain intact.
frames.key_state: Popped right 7, 3, and root 1 in order to complete the three final backtracking steps; path = [], res = [[1, 7], [1, 3, 7]].
frames.announcement: Exit right 7, node 3, and root 1 in order; path is now empty and the search is complete.
